# 1 Enoch Chapter 72 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** This is the record of how the lights of heaven move — their patterns, their categories, their authority over different seasons, what they are called, where they originate, and how they govern the months. Uriel, the holy angel who accompanied me as their heavenly guide, showed me all of this. He revealed their exact laws and explained how all the years of the world will unfold, right up to the moment when a new creation — one that lasts forever — is completed.

**2** Here is the first principle governing the luminaries: the Sun rises through the eastern gates of heaven and sets through the western gates.

**3** I counted six gates through which the sun rises and six gates through which it sets. The moon likewise rises and sets through these same gates, and so do the star-leaders and their followers — six on the east side, six on the west, each following the other in perfect order. Alongside these gates are many windows on both sides.

**4** The great luminary — the Sun — sets out first. It travels in a great arc across the sky, moving westward for a hundred and eighty days before it sets.

**5** During that stretch of time, the days lengthen and the nights shorten. The day ends up one-tenth longer than the night.

**6** The day lasts ten time-parts and the night lasts eight.

**7** The sun rises from the third gate, tracks west and sets through the third western gate, and maintains this for thirty-one days before shifting to set through the second gate.

**8** During that period the nights grow longer and the days shorter, until by the thirtieth morning the day is ten parts and the night is eight parts.

**9** When the sun sets, the moon — ruler of the night — begins its journey. Throughout this period the night keeps lengthening and the day keeps shrinking.

**10** Eventually the night reaches nine parts and the day nine parts — they are perfectly equal.

**11** Night and day stand equal at nine parts each.

**12** The sun then rises from that gate and sets in the west, swings back east, and rises through the fourth gate for thirty-one mornings before setting in the western sky.

**13** Day by day the days grow longer and night by night the nights grow shorter, all the way to the thirtieth morning.

**14** At that point the day is ten parts and the night eight parts.

**15** The sun rises from that gate, sets through the fifth western gate for thirty days, then rises through the fifth gate and sets through the fifth gate in the west.

**16** The days keep getting longer and the nights shorter, until the day stretches to eleven parts and the night shrinks to seven.

**17** The sun loops back east and enters the sixth gate, rising and setting through the sixth gate for thirty-one days as marked by its sign.

**18** Now the day surpasses the night — the day is twice as long as the night — twelve parts to six.

**19** Then the sun begins to rise in a way that shortens the day and lengthens the night; it returns to the east and enters the sixth gate, rising and setting there for another thirty days.

**20** The days now grow shorter and the nights longer — by thirty days the day is ten parts and the night is eight.

**21** The sun leaves the sixth gate, sets in the west, then heads back east and rises through the fifth gate for thirty days before setting in the west again.

**22** The day is eleven parts, the night seven.

**23** The sun leaves the fifth gate and sets through the fifth western gate, then rises through the fourth gate for thirty-one days according to its sign before setting in the west.

**24** Now the day and night balance out again — perfectly equal — nine parts each.

**25** The sun rises from the fourth gate, sets through the fourth gate, swings back east, and rises through the third gate for thirty-one mornings before setting in the western sky.

**26** Now the nights grow longer than the days — the night is double the day — ten parts to eight.

**27** The sun rises from the third gate, sets through the third western gate, swings east again, and rises through the second eastern gate for thirty mornings before setting through the second western gate.

**28** The night is now eleven parts and the day only seven.

**29** The sun swings back east and enters the first gate, setting through the first western gate for thirty-one mornings.

**30** The nights grow even longer, reaching double the length of the day — twelve parts of night to six of day.

**31** The sun has now completed its circuit through all the gates and begins its return journey. It passes through that gate for thirty mornings and sets in the west opposite.

**32** That night, the night begins to shorten by one-ninth. The night is eleven parts and the day seven.

**33** The sun swings back and enters the second eastern gate, working its way along these divisions for thirty mornings, rising and setting.

**34** The nights keep shrinking — until the night is nine parts and the day nine parts, equal once again.

**35** The complete year runs exactly three hundred and sixty-four days.

**36** The differences in the lengths of days and nights all come from the sun's journey through its gates.

**37** As the sun travels, the days gradually grow longer and the nights gradually shorter — and all of this is governed by the sun's path through its gates.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering aimed at modern English readability. The Astronomical Book encodes a 364-day solar calendar with enormous significance for Second Temple Judaism — it is the calendar used at Qumran and apparently by the authors of Jubilees. The six "portals" or gates represent different positions of sunrise/sunset along the horizon across the seasons, reflecting ancient astronomical observation rather than a heliocentric model.*
